summary: Verified iter16 batch (5 fixes). FIX#1/#2/#3/#5 PASS. FIX#4 visfAtlas: atlas loads + crosshair-info column appears, but the registered categorical 'visfAtlas' colormap is NOT applied — overlay falls back to 'gray' so all ROIs render the same color instead of distinct hues. Race condition between async fetch of visfAtlas_colormap.json and overlay attach.

ui_bugs.issue: Custom categorical 'visfAtlas' cmap registered via fetch().then(addColormap) — but when the user toggles visfAtlas overlay before the fetch resolves (or the overlay is attached before the cmap exists), niivue falls back to the 'gray' colormap. The COLORMAP dropdown in the visfAtlas layer panel shows 'gray', and the brain renders all 33 ROIs as a single monochromatic blue blob instead of 33 distinct categorical colors as required by spec.

integration_issues.issue: Race: fetch('/atlases/visfAtlas_colormap.json').then(cm => nv.addColormap('visfAtlas', cm)) at niivue init may not finish before user toggles the atlas. Need to (a) await the fetch before drawScene/overlay attach, OR (b) re-call setColormap after overlay loads, OR (c) bundle the cmap statically like buildPolarAngleCmap() in InflatedBrainViewer.

action_items: FIX#4 ROOT CAUSE: In /app/frontend/src/components/NiivueViewer.jsx lines ~109-112, the fetch('/atlases/visfAtlas_colormap.json').then(cm => nv.addColormap('visfAtlas', cm)) registers the cmap asynchronously. When user clicks toggle-visfAtlas before the fetch completes, niivue attaches the overlay with colormap='visfAtlas' but the name isn't registered yet — it silently falls back to 'gray'. RECOMMENDED FIX: either (a) bundle the cmap inline at module load (same pattern used by buildPolarAngleCmap in InflatedBrainViewer.jsx) so it's available synchronously, (b) await the fetch in the init promise and ensure addColormap runs before any user-initiated overlay add, or (c) after each overlay add, if colormap===visfAtlas, re-issue nv.setColormap(volId, 'visfAtlas') once the registered map is confirmed present and call nv.updateGLVolume()/drawScene(). Option (a) is simplest given the cmap JSON is only ~2.3KB.
critical_code_review_comments: InflatedBrainViewer.jsx cleanup (lines 98-101): The useEffect cleanup sets cancelled=true and nullifies nvRef but does NOT call nv.gl?.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context')?.loseContext() or remove the canvas event listeners. Each toggle of Interactive 3D creates a new Niivue instance bound to a fresh canvas — over many toggles this leaks WebGL contexts. Most browsers cap at ~16 active contexts before refusing new ones.

InflatedBrainViewer.jsx line 89-90: if (cancelled) return BEFORE loadMeshes — good. But there's no equivalent check AFTER loadMeshes completes / before drawScene. If the user toggles fast, drawScene can be called on a disposed nv.
NiivueViewer.jsx visfAtlas cmap (lines 109-112): No error logging on fetch failure beyond catch swallow. Recommend a console.warn so future debug catches the race.

atlasConfig.js line 146 ('colormap: visfAtlas'): Pairs with the async registration above — if the cmap name is unknown to niivue at overlay-add time, niivue silently falls back to default rather than warning. Consider validating cmap availability in the layer add path.

rca of the issue: FIX#4 visfAtlas: NiivueViewer.jsx registers the custom categorical 'visfAtlas' colormap via an unawaited fetch promise inside the niivue init effect. The user can toggle the atlas before the fetch resolves; niivue accepts the overlay with colormap='visfAtlas' but since the name isn't yet registered in cmapper, it silently falls back to the default ('gray'). Reproduction: load page → immediately expand ATLASES (within ~1s of page load) → click toggle-visfAtlas → COLORMAP dropdown shows 'gray', overlay renders as a single hue. Mitigation: bundle the cmap inline (like buildPolarAngleCmap() in InflatedBrainViewer) so registration is synchronous; alternative is to await the fetch in the init sequence.
